en: Itivuttaka 79 Tikanipāta,
Third Chapter (Tatiyavagga)
The Discourse on Decline.
This was said by the Blessed One; thus have I heard:
“Bhikkhus, there are these three things that lead to the decline of a bhikkhu in training.
Which three?
Here, monks, a bhikkhu who is still in training delights in work, takes delight in work, and is devoted to delighting in work;
he delights in talk, takes delight in talk, and is devoted to delighting in talk.
He delights in sleep, is fond of sleep, and is devoted to the pleasure of sleep.
These, monks, are the three qualities that lead to the decline of a monk in training.
There are, monks, these three qualities that lead to the non-decline of a monk in training.
Which three?
Here, monks, a bhikkhu in training does not delight in work, does not rejoice in work, and is not devoted to delighting in work;
he does not delight in talk, does not rejoice in talk, and is not devoted to delighting in talk.
“He does not delight in sleep, he does not crave sleep, and he is not devoted to the pleasure of sleep.
These, monks, are the three qualities that lead to the non-decline of a monk in training.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
“Delighting in work, delighting in talk,
and delighting in sleep, one who is restless;”
Such a bhikkhu is incapable of touching the supreme enlightenment;
therefore, one should be of few duties.
Free from sloth and unagitated—
that kind of bhikkhu is capable of touching the supreme enlightenment.
This meaning too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The tenth [sutta].
The third chapter.
Its summary verse:
Two views, escape, form,
a son, and [the simile] with the lack of rain.
"The element of pleasure is fragile;
these ten [qualities] are lost through decline."
